claims.statement: IncidentReport is the agent's output for one fault, with symptom/affected_resource/namespace/severity fields, a list of Hypothesis candidate causes, blast_radius and upstream_unhealthy, structured evidence, suggested_next_steps, and a reasoning_mode provenance field.

A Hypothesis carries a cause, a human-readable evidence_chain, a confidence score from 0.0 to 1.0, and supporting evidence; Evidence has a category and citations; a Citation points to the primary evidence (log, metric/PromQL, event, runbook, graph, or change).

The service-anchored model resolves a fault to a stable anchor in priority order service, then owning workload, then pod, records the pods behind it in affected_pods, and is verified by anchor tests that prefer the service and fall back to workload then pod.
The anchor deduplicates sibling pods: five pods behind one Service that fail identically produce a single service-anchored incident listing all the pods rather than one incident per pod.
upstream_unhealthy is the candidate-cause side (dependencies via calls edges that are themselves unhealthy) and blast_radius is the downstream impact side of the graph walk.

An incident is created active and reconcile_status flips it to inactive with resolved_at set only when every pod in affected_pods is healthy again in the current graph (strict recovery), where a pod missing from the graph counts as recovered.

related_incidents is a deterministic pattern flag linking incidents with the same failure signature on a different resource within the correlation window, and it never changes hypothesis confidence or claims what the shared cause is.

When reconcile_status resolves an incident it clears the status-detection latches for its pods (discards each from _status_incident_open and removes its _unhealthy_streak entry) so the same pod can re-fire a fresh incident if it breaks again.

Anchor dedup (_merge_into_open_anchor) merges sibling pods that share the same service or workload anchor into one open incident and applies only to service/workload anchors, while correlation (_correlate) links different anchors sharing an identical blanked failure signature within the correlation window.
